note: The re-test engine's spec registry (god's-eye panel build 3, task 25; Sig, Oct 27 2026). Read by scripts/insight_engine.py. APPEND ONLY: a spec is fixed before its data is read and is never edited. To change anything about a test, add a new spec with a new id and leave the old one here; it stays counted in the ledger-wide correction. The engine stores each spec's hash with every result and refuses a spec whose hash moved. sig_yes is the only field that may change (Sig's yes, a date) and it is left out of the hash. Nothing in this file or in the results is ever published by the engine.

ledger_prior.why: Tests already spent before this registry: about 137 from vision-2026-10-22 plus about 13 from the god's-eye panel (relationships.md, Oct 27). Every spec below counts on top of these, including ones that re-ask a panel question, because no panel spec file survives to show they are the same test (seats/10-skeptic.md D1).

barge3.what: Mean of the St. Louis, Mid-Mississippi and Lower Illinois barge rates (percent of tariff), at least 2 of 3 that week
barge3.release_note: Tuesday rate, out Thursday in the Grain Transportation Report

checked.facts: Grain Transportation Report of Thursday Oct 22, 2026, Table 9: St. Louis rate dated Tuesday 10/20/2026. Matches obs Tuesday and the 2-day lag. One issue checked; holiday weeks not verified.
checked.data_check: history/agtransport/barge_rates: every St. Louis row (563) is dated a Tuesday.

gulf_corn.what: Corn basis, Gulf - Louisiana, 30-day to arrive, cents per bushel
gulf_corn.release_note: Conservative, and the Oct 22, 2026 report matches it (see checked): a Friday basis is taken as known only on the next Thursday's report

checked.facts: The same Oct 22, 2026 issue, Table 2a, prints the corn IL-Gulf spread for Friday 10/16/2026 and 10/9/2026: a Friday basis first appears in the next Thursday's report, the 6-day lag used here. One issue checked; holiday weeks not verified.
checked.sign: Table 2a's label is IL-Gulf (Illinois basis minus Gulf basis): 10/9/2026 is -1.06, and history/agtransport/grain_basis gives Illinois -0.338 and Gulf - Louisiana 0.722 that day, the same -1.06. spread_gulf_interior is the other way round, Gulf minus interior, so a wider Gulf premium is a larger number.

interior_corn.what: Mean of the Illinois and Iowa corn elevator bid basis, both needed, cents per bushel

spread_gulf_interior.what: gulf_corn minus interior_corn, same Friday, cents

gulf_corn_inspections.what: Corn export inspections, AMS region GULF, thousand metric tons per week
gulf_corn_inspections.release_note: Week ending Thursday, released the next Monday

basis_log_corn.release_note: public the day it is logged

specs.title: Rival contagion as seat 4 ran it: rivals 25 mi or less vs rivals 100 to 300 mi
specs.x: Elevator e moves its corn basis on trading day t (sign of the summed change over its corn bids that day)
specs.y: A rival r (other company, did not move on day t) moves its corn basis the same way on t+1 to t+3; first move in that window counts
specs.trading_days: weekdays with a basis log file; weekend files are left out
specs.estimate: net = (near same - near opposite) / near pairs minus the same for control pairs, percentage points
specs.placebo: shuffle which facility's change series sits at which location, within state
else_explains: shared parent co-op or bid vendor
a board refreshed on the next poll, not repriced (posted is a batch time)
local harvest pace
a regional trend: the 100 to 300 mi control is another region (skeptic D1)

specs.title: A barge rate change leads the next week's change in the Gulf minus interior corn spread

specs.title: Corn good plus excellent at NASS week 30 beats the state trend for final state yield
specs.lag: rating released the Monday after week 30, long before the final yield
specs.model: expanding window: per-state linear trend on every earlier yield year, plus one pooled slope on the rating's distance from that state's earlier mean
specs.benchmark: the state trend alone (same expanding window)
specs.placebo: shuffle ratings across states within each holdout year
else_explains: a short trend window that holds 2012 sets the slope
ratings track what the trend already knows

specs.benchmark: the state trend alone (same expanding window)
specs.placebo: shuffle ratings across states within each holdout year

ratings track what the trend already knows
drought years (1988, 2012) set the slope
